title: Comparatives 2
note: PULLED FORWARD from B2 (James dropdown 2026-09-02) - the tree files this at B2.comparatives.advanced, but as...as is common well below that. Builds on a2_comparatives / a2_superlatives. Czech tak...jako gives *as tall like me. Second job: the modifier slot before a comparative (much / far / a bit), where very is the target error. Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): 15 new, balanced across the four shapes - as ... as, not as ... as, less / the least, and the modifier slot (much / far / a bit) where *very better* and *more easier* are the target errors. Rules applied this pass: F4 was a false positive on She's / It's - the subject contraction moved out of `en` into accepts, which also cleared both F3 leads; A8 twins closed; A4 both cleared (The train -> A train, and the Czech demonstrative on `ta nejlevnejsi moznost`, where `the` is the taught form and not an accident); F3 `crowded` swapped for `expensive`. Every option list carries this unit's own errors - like for as, very before a comparative, more + -er, and least without the.

cards.title: As tall as
points: You already know **-er /** more and **the -est** / the most.
These are the other ways to compare. Czech **tak… jako** becomes **as… as**, not *as… like*.

examples.cz: Je stejně vysoká jako její bratr.

examples.en: This flat isn't **as expensive** as the other one.
examples.cz: Tenhle byt není tak drahý jako ten druhý.

cards.title: less and the least
points: **less** works with any adjective, but for short ones people usually say **not as**.

rows: **not as** crowded — more common in speech

cards.title: much better, not very better
points: **very** goes with a plain adjective: very good. Never with a comparative.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: **as …** as for equal, and **much /** far / a bit before a comparative.

rows: ~~It's not so expensive as the other one.~~
It's **not as** expensive as the other one.

items.en: She is as tall as her brother.
items.cz: Je stejně vysoká jako její bratr.
items.gap: She is as tall ____ her brother. (as / like)
accepts: She is as tall as her brother.
She's as tall as her brother.
items.wrong: She is as tall like her brother.
items.explanation: The pair is **as … as**. Czech *jako* is not *like* here.
items.explanation_cz: Dvojice je **as … as**. České *jako* tady není *like*.

items.en: This flat isn't as expensive as the other one.
items.cz: Tenhle byt není tak drahý jako ten druhý.
items.gap: This flat isn't ____ expensive as the other one. (as / so)
accepts: This flat isn't as expensive as the other one.
This flat is not as expensive as the other one.
items.explanation: Negative equal: **not as** … as.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná rovnost: **not as** … as.

items.en: This one is much better.
items.cz: Tenhle je mnohem lepší.
items.gap: This one is ____ better. (much / very)
accepts: This one is much better.
items.wrong: This one is very better.
items.explanation: **much** goes before a comparative. **very** does not.
items.explanation_cz: **much** stojí před 2. stupněm. **very** ne.

items.en: A train is far cheaper than a plane.
items.cz: Vlak je mnohem levnější než letadlo.
items.gap: A train is ____ cheaper than a plane. (far / very)
accepts: A train is far cheaper than a plane.
items.explanation: **far** + comparative, like much.
items.explanation_cz: **far** + 2. stupeň, stejně jako much.
items.wrong: A train is very cheaper than a plane.

items.en: My flat is less expensive than yours.
items.cz: Můj byt je míň drahý než tvůj.
items.gap: My flat is ____ expensive than yours. (less / least)
accepts: My flat is less expensive than yours.
items.explanation: **less** + adjective + than for the smaller amount.
items.explanation_cz: **less** + přídavné jméno + than pro menší míru.
items.wrong: My flat is least expensive than yours.

items.en: It is a bit longer than I expected.
items.cz: Je to trochu delší, než jsem čekal.
items.gap: It is ____ longer than I expected. (a bit / very)
accepts: It is a bit longer than I expected.
It's a bit longer than I expected.
items.explanation: **a bit** softens a comparative.
items.explanation_cz: **a bit** zjemňuje 2. stupeň.
items.wrong: It is very longer than I expected.

items.en: He isn't as fast as he used to be.
items.cz: Není tak rychlý, jak býval.
items.gap: He isn't ____ fast as he used to be. (as / so)
accepts: He isn't as fast as he used to be.
He is not as fast as he used to be.
items.explanation: **not as** fast as — the standard negative equal.
items.explanation_cz: **not as** fast as — běžná záporná rovnost.

items.en: This is the least expensive option.
items.cz: Tohle je ta nejlevnější možnost.
items.gap: This is ____ expensive option. (the least / less)
accepts: This is the least expensive option.
items.explanation: **the least** + adjective for the bottom of the group.
items.explanation_cz: **the least** + přídavné jméno pro nejnižší ve skupině.

items.en: Prague is much bigger than Brno.
items.cz: Praha je mnohem větší než Brno.
items.gap: Prague is ____ bigger than Brno. (much / very)
accepts: Prague is much bigger than Brno.
items.wrong: Prague is more bigger than Brno.
items.explanation: **much** bigger. Never *very bigger*, never *more bigger*.
items.explanation_cz: **much** bigger. Nikdy *very bigger*, nikdy *more bigger*.

items.en: Her new job is as good as the old one.
items.cz: Její nová práce je stejně dobrá jako ta stará.
items.gap: Her new job is ____ good as the old one. (as / so)
accepts: Her new job is as good as the old one.
items.explanation: **as good as** — the two are equal.
items.explanation_cz: **as good as** — obě jsou stejné.

items.en: This book is not as good as the film.
items.cz: Ta kniha není tak dobrá jako ten film.
items.gap: This book is not ____ good as the film. (as / so)
accepts: This book is not as good as the film.
This book isn't as good as the film.
items.wrong: This book is not so good as the film.
items.explanation: The equal frame is **as … as**, and the negative keeps both words: not **as** good **as**.
items.explanation_cz: Vazba pro rovnost je **as … as** a zápor obě slova nechává: not **as** good **as**.

items.en: My new phone is much faster than the old one.
items.cz: Můj nový telefon je mnohem rychlejší než ten starý.
items.gap: My new phone is ____ faster than the old one. (much / very)
accepts: My new phone is much faster than the old one.
items.wrong: My new phone is very faster than the old one.
items.explanation: **much** goes in front of a comparative. *very* only goes with a plain adjective: very fast.
items.explanation_cz: **much** stojí před druhým stupněm. *very* patří jen k prostému přídavnému jménu: very fast.

items.en: She is as old as my sister.
items.cz: Je stejně stará jako moje sestra.
items.gap: She is as old ____ my sister. (as / like)
accepts: She is as old as my sister.
She's as old as my sister.
items.wrong: She is as old like my sister.
items.explanation: Czech *jako* is **as** here, not *like*. The frame is as + adjective + **as**.
items.explanation_cz: České *jako* je tady **as**, ne *like*. Vazba je as + přídavné jméno + **as**.

items.en: This exam was much easier than the last one.
items.cz: Ta zkouška byla mnohem lehčí než ta minulá.
items.gap: This exam was ____ easier than the last one. (much / very)
accepts: This exam was much easier than the last one.
items.wrong: This exam was more easier than the last one.
items.explanation: One comparative is enough: **much easier**, never *more easier*.
items.explanation_cz: Jeden druhý stupeň stačí: **much easier**, nikdy *more easier*.

items.en: Our flat is not as big as theirs.
items.cz: Náš byt není tak velký jako jejich.
items.gap: Our flat is not ____ big as theirs. (as / so)
accepts: Our flat is not as big as theirs.
Our flat isn't as big as theirs.
items.wrong: Our flat is not so big as theirs.
items.explanation: **not as … as** says the first one is less. *not so big as* is old-fashioned.
items.explanation_cz: **not as … as** říká, že ten první je menší. *not so big as* je zastaralé.

items.en: He is not as young as he looks.
items.cz: Není tak mladý, jak vypadá.
items.gap: He is not ____ young as he looks. (as / so)
accepts: He is not as young as he looks.
He isn't as young as he looks.
items.wrong: He is not as young like he looks.
items.explanation: Both halves of the frame stay: not **as** young **as**.
items.explanation_cz: Obě části vazby zůstávají: not **as** young **as**.

items.en: The second film was far better than the first.
items.cz: Ten druhý film byl mnohem lepší než ten první.
items.gap: The second film was ____ better than the first. (far / very)
accepts: The second film was far better than the first.
items.wrong: The second film was very better than the first.
items.explanation: **far** is another word for *much* in front of a comparative. *very better* is not English.
items.explanation_cz: **far** je před druhým stupněm další slovo pro *much*. *very better* není angličtina.

items.en: My job is less interesting than yours.
items.cz: Moje práce je míň zajímavá než tvoje.
items.gap: My job is ____ interesting than yours. (less / least)
accepts: My job is less interesting than yours.
items.wrong: My job is least interesting than yours.
items.explanation: **less** compares two things. *the least* is for the bottom of a whole group.
items.explanation_cz: **less** porovnává dvě věci. *the least* je pro nejnižší z celé skupiny.

items.en: This hotel is a bit cheaper than the other one.
items.cz: Tenhle hotel je trochu levnější než ten druhý.
items.gap: This hotel is ____ cheaper than the other one. (a bit / very)
accepts: This hotel is a bit cheaper than the other one.
items.wrong: This hotel is very cheaper than the other one.
items.explanation: **a bit** is the small-difference modifier. It sits in the same slot as much and far.
items.explanation_cz: **a bit** je zesilovač pro malý rozdíl. Stojí na stejném místě jako much a far.

items.en: Their house is much older than ours.
items.cz: Jejich dům je mnohem starší než náš.
items.gap: Their house is ____ older than ours. (much / very)
accepts: Their house is much older than ours.
items.wrong: Their house is very older than ours.
items.explanation: **much older** — very never stands in front of a comparative.
items.explanation_cz: **much older** — very před druhým stupněm nikdy nestojí.

items.en: I am not as tired as I was yesterday.
items.cz: Nejsem tak unavený jako včera.
items.gap: I am not ____ tired as I was yesterday. (as / so)
accepts: I am not as tired as I was yesterday.
I'm not as tired as I was yesterday.
items.wrong: I am not as tired like I was yesterday.
items.explanation: The second **as** is the one Czech speakers drop or turn into *like*.
items.explanation_cz: To druhé **as** je právě to, co Češi vynechávají nebo mění na *like*.

items.en: It was the least interesting film I have seen.
items.cz: Byl to ten nejmíň zajímavý film, co jsem viděl.
items.gap: It was ____ interesting film I have seen. (the least / less)
accepts: It was the least interesting film I have seen.
It was the least interesting film I've seen.
items.wrong: It was less interesting film I have seen.
items.explanation: The bottom of a group takes **the least**, with *the*, exactly like the most.
items.explanation_cz: Nejnižší ze skupiny má **the least**, se členem *the*, přesně jako the most.

items.en: The new office is much smaller than the old one.
items.cz: Ta nová kancelář je mnohem menší než ta stará.
items.gap: The new office is ____ smaller than the old one. (much / very)
accepts: The new office is much smaller than the old one.
items.wrong: The new office is more smaller than the old one.
items.explanation: **much smaller**: one comparative, one modifier, and never *more* with -er.
items.explanation_cz: **much smaller**: jeden druhý stupeň, jeden zesilovač a nikdy *more* s -er.

items.en: Her English is as good as mine.
items.cz: Její angličtina je stejně dobrá jako moje.
items.gap: Her English is as good ____ mine. (as / like)
accepts: Her English is as good as mine.
items.wrong: Her English is as good like mine.
items.explanation: Equal means **as … as**, whatever the noun is.
items.explanation_cz: Rovnost je **as … as**, ať je podstatné jméno jakékoli.

items.en: This is the least useful book on my desk.
items.cz: Tohle je ta nejmíň užitečná kniha na mém stole.
items.gap: This is ____ useful book on my desk. (the least / less)
accepts: This is the least useful book on my desk.
items.wrong: This is less useful book on my desk.
items.explanation: **the least** picks the bottom one out of everything on the desk.
items.explanation_cz: **the least** vybírá tu úplně nejnižší ze všeho na stole.
